## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Agent details

Written with Claude Code: the analysis, measurements and test plan below.

**TLDR:** The CP-16 LoRA SFT recipe moves from Ulysses flex on FA4 (256-token blocks) to Ulysses `varlen`, pinned to FA4. The Muse Ulysses CP transform now maps the varlen global and sliding-window layers. Attention kernel time per 128k step drops by 16% on one document and by 25-30% when the 128k tokens hold 4-8 documents (the recipe packs up to 8). Step time was not measured. The shared 816B builder still defaults to flex, so the Dist-MoE scale recipes keep it.

```text
CP-16 LoRA SFT, one rank (8 q / 1 kv heads, the full sequence after the Ulysses all-to-all)
main:     global + window layers -> flex, FA4 backend, 256-token block mask
this PR:  global layers          -> varlen, FA4 (cuDNN is slower here, Results)
          window layers          -> varlen, FA4 with its native 2048 window
```

```python
# before
config = _muse_spark_816b_a42b(seq_len=seq_len, parallelism=...)
...
for _, inner_attention, _, _ in config.model.traverse(FlexInnerAttention.Config):
    inner_attention.kernel_options = {"BACKEND": "FLASH"}
    inner_attention.block_size = 256
# after
config = _muse_spark_816b_a42b(seq_len=seq_len, parallelism=..., attn_backend="varlen")
...
for _, inner_attention, _, _ in config.model.traverse(VarlenInnerAttention.Config):
    inner_attention.sdpa_backends = [SDPBackend.FLASH_ATTENTION]
```

**Stack** (merge bottom-up; this PR is in **bold**)

| # | PR | Independent? | Needs (stack positions) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #5704 vLLM generator: decode-specialized FULL graphs for every model, DP>1-safe | yes | — |
| 2 | #5490 FULL CUDA graphs for linear-attention generators at DP>1 | no | 1 |
| 3 | #5489 vLLM generator: 128-token KV pages when FA4 runs attention | yes | — |
| **4** | **this PR: Muse Spark: use varlen attention in the CP-16 LoRA SFT recipe** | **yes** | **—** |

**Problem**
1. **Layers.** The 816B model has 16 global and 46 sliding-window (2048) layers: head dim 64, 128 q / 16 kv heads.
2. **Flex only.** The shared 816B builder, `_muse_spark_816b_a42b`, hard-codes `attn_backend="flex"`. The CP-16 LoRA SFT recipe then puts every flex layer on its FA4 backend with 256-token blocks.
3. **Window layers.** Flex passes the window to FA4 as a 256-token block mask plus a mask function on the partial blocks. Varlen hands the window to FA4 directly. At the recipe's per-rank shape, flex's window layers take 1.7x varlen's time (Results).

**Solution**
1. `_muse_spark_816b_a42b` takes `attn_backend` (default `"flex"`, so other callers don't change). The CP-16 LoRA recipe passes `"varlen"`.
2. The Muse Ulysses transform maps `VarlenInnerAttention` and `SlidingWindowVarlenInnerAttention` to their Ulysses versions. The transform matches exact types (`config/transform/context_parallel.py:60-64`), so both entries are needed.
3. The CP-16 LoRA recipe pins its varlen layers to FA4. torch's default order puts the global layers on cuDNN, which is 1% slower than flex on one 128k document and 13% slower than FA4.
4. The recipe's flex FA4 loop goes away. With varlen decoder layers it would only reach the vision encoder, which this text-only recipe skips (`dataset_modalities` is empty).
5. Unchanged: the builder's default, the Dist-MoE scale recipes, the debug recipes and every RL recipe.

**Results**
```text
Numerics: not bitwise: different kernels, same masks (per-document causal, 2048 window).
          rel L2 vs fp32, one layer, 8 x 16k                 out      dq       dk       dv
          global, flex FA4 (main)                            2.1e-3   2.5e-3   2.4e-3   2.3e-3
          global, varlen FA4 (this PR)                       2.1e-3   2.5e-3   2.4e-3   2.3e-3
          window, flex FA4 and varlen FA4                    2.2e-3   2.4e-3   2.4e-3   2.3e-3
          Muse Spark debug model, 2 GPUs, 3 training steps (activation checkpointing off), flex (Triton) vs varlen with cuDNN global layers (default order):
          layout              tokens   loss rel diff   grad-norm rel diff   step-1 grads rel L2
          TP 2 + EP 2 + SP    16k      <= 4.2e-5       <= 6.4e-4            2.0e-2
                              32k      <= 3.5e-5       <= 3.2e-4            1.4e-2
          Ulysses CP 2 + EP 2 16k      <= 9.7e-5       <= 5.0e-4            2.1e-2
                              32k      <= 2.9e-5       <= 7.2e-4            1.5e-2
          yardstick, TP 2, 16k: Triton flex vs flex on FA4 (two flex kernels)                       1.9e-2
          The recipe's path: Ulysses CP 2 + EP 1, varlen FA4, max_num_documents 8, 16k, deterministic, 6 steps,
          CUDA graphs on vs off: loss and grad norm bitwise at every step on both ranks. Steps 1-2 are eager warmup,
          step 3 captures, steps 4-6 replay the graph on new microbatches.

Kernel time per 128k microbatch (= one step: num_tokens_per_train_step = 131072), 16 global + 46 window layers.
Step time not measured: this excludes the Ulysses all-to-alls and the MoE. Attention is saved, not recomputed (muse_spark.py:94).
documents    main (flex FA4)    this PR (varlen FA4)    delta              varlen with cuDNN global (not chosen)
1 x 128k     1116 ms            936 ms                  -179 ms  -16.1%    1046 ms  -6.3%
4 x 32k       441 ms            331 ms                  -110 ms  -25.0%     365 ms  -17.3%
8 x 16k       319 ms            222 ms                   -97 ms  -30.4%     237 ms  -25.7%

Per layer, fwd+bwd, eager, GB300, ms, min of 2 rounds; 8 q / 1 kv heads, head dim 64, window 2048;
varlen metadata fixed as under CUDA graphs: 8 document slots, max_context_length 131072, no padding segment
(the recipe's packer adds one padding segment: 9 slots)
documents    global: flex FA4   varlen cuDNN   varlen FA4      window: flex FA4   varlen FA4
1 x 128k             57.72      58.34          51.49                    4.18       2.44
4 x 32k              15.47      15.64          13.50                    4.20       2.49
8 x 16k               8.48       8.04           7.11                    3.99       2.36
```
Decode and prefill: not touched (training recipe only).

You may ask: why not keep flex on FA4 for every Muse recipe? It's one backend, but the window layers, 46 of 62, take 1.7x longer on it.
You may ask: why not varlen in the Dist-MoE scale recipes too? Three things block it today:
- Their C4 loader sets no `max_num_documents`. Under CUDA graphs, validation raises for any varlen layer without it (`config/validation.py:111-118`).
- Their CP is K/V all-gather. Varlen K/V all-gather is untested on Muse.
- `_use_flex_flash_attention` raises on any non-flex layer (`torchtitan_recipes/models/muse_spark.py:223`).

NOTE: kernel times only. Not run: the CP-16 LoRA recipe itself (16 GPUs), its step time and its loss curve.

**Follow up**
- [ ] CP-16 LoRA SFT, a few steps on 16 GPUs: loss and step time, main vs this PR.
- [ ] Varlen K/V all-gather CP for the Dist-MoE scale recipes: a document cap on their loader and a step-time comparison against flex.

**Test plan**
- New CPU test `test_cp16_lora_recipe_uses_ulysses_varlen` builds the CP-16 recipe and checks that every decoder layer is Ulysses varlen. It fails on main.
- Built every Muse recipe and ran `validate_model_training_config` (it runs `validate_context_parallel`): all pass, except the MXFP8 debug recipe, which needs a torchao nightly to build (an import error, same on main). Only the CP-16 LoRA recipe changes: 16 global + 46 window layers move from Ulysses flex to Ulysses varlen.
- 2-GPU debug-model training, flex vs varlen, TP 2 + EP 2 + SP and Ulysses CP 2 + EP 2, 16k and 32k tokens, 3 steps. Losses are within 1e-4, and step-1 grads differ by the same rel L2 as swapping one flex kernel for another (numbers above). Activation checkpointing was off: with it on, the TP 2 layout fails in backward on main too.
- 2-GPU run of the recipe's path: Ulysses CP 2, varlen pinned to FA4, `max_num_documents` 8, deterministic, 6 steps, CUDA graphs on vs off. Loss and grad norm are bitwise equal at every step, including the 3 replays on new microbatches; the graphs run logs "Recorded CUDA graph forward_backward" on each rank.
- CPU: `tests/unit_tests/cpu/recipes`, `tests/rl/unit_tests/cpu`: same failures as main, all others pass. pre-commit passes, pyrefly included.

**Claude finished @felipemello1's task in 2m 57s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/40956574403)

---
**Approve -- please address the items below before merging** (one comment fix, an optional `Literal` signature tidy-up, and a question about running the recipe on 16 GPUs before merge). See the [review](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5706#pullrequestreview).

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** The change touches only the recipe, it is the smallest way to get varlen into the CP-16 LoRA recipe, and the kernel evidence supports it. The only open point is the 16-GPU run, which belongs to the author or a maintainer.

**What this PR does.** `_muse_spark_816b_a42b` now takes an `attn_backend` argument. The CP-16 LoRA SFT recipe passes `"varlen"` and pins every varlen layer to `SDPBackend.FLASH_ATTENTION`, which is FA4 on sm100. The Muse Ulysses CP map gains entries for `VarlenInnerAttention` and `SlidingWindowVarlenInnerAttention`. Without them, `ContextParallelTransform.transform` raises "No CP inner attention configured", because it looks up the exact owner type. The recipe no longer sets the flex FA4 `kernel_options` and `block_size`. After this change, the only flex attention left in the model is the vision encoder's (`flavors.py:560`), and this text-only recipe never runs it.

**Example.**
```text
recipe: muse_spark_816b_a42b_ultradata_lora_sft_cp16_128k (CP 16, EP 16, Ulysses)
before: layers[*].attention.inner_attention = UlyssesFlexInnerAttention / UlyssesSlidingWindowFlexInnerAttention
        kernel_options={"BACKEND": "FLASH"}, block_size=256
after:  layers[*].attention.inner_attention = UlyssesVarlenInnerAttention / UlyssesSlidingWindowVarlenInnerAttention
        sdpa_backends=[FLASH_ATTENTION]; window layers get window_size=(2047, 0) passed straight to FA4
other recipes calling _muse_spark_816b_a42b: unchanged (still flex)
```

### Must fix
- `torchtitan_recipes/models/muse_spark.py:836`: the comment blames torch for the cuDNN-first order, but the order comes from torchtitan's own `VarlenInnerAttention.Config` default (inline comment).

### Should consider
- `torchtitan_recipes/models/muse_spark.py:325`: type `attn_backend` as `Literal["flex", "varlen"]` and drop the default, since there are only two callers (inline comment).

### Questions
- Will the 16-GPU CP-16 LoRA run (loss and step time, main vs. this PR) happen before merge? Today the recipe's numerics change rests on per-layer kernel comparisons plus 2-GPU debug-model runs. CLAUDE.md asks for loss convergence on computation changes, and that run is the one direct check of the recipe that actually ships.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Ulysses varlen: after the all-to-all, each rank holds the full sequence for its head shard, so the document-causal and window metadata are the same as without CP. Under CUDA graphs, varlen needs `max_num_documents`, and the UltraData loader sets it to 8 (`muse_spark.py:697`).
- The `traverse(VarlenInnerAttention.Config)` loop matches subclasses. That includes both Ulysses varlen configs and the sliding-window variant, so all 62 decoder layers get pinned.
- The remat save region `attention.inner_attention` is matched by FQN, so attention is still saved, not recomputed, after the backend change.
- The new CPU test is the only one that builds this recipe, and the build is where a missing CP-map entry would raise. That part of the test earns its cost.

</details>

Not verified: the GPU kernel times and the numerics. I couldn't run the new CPU test in this environment either. CPU CI was skipped because the base branch isn't `main`.

The cuDNN-first order isn't torch's default. It's torchtitan's own `VarlenInnerAttention.Config.sdpa_backends` default, `[CUDNN_ATTENTION, FLASH_ATTENTION]` (`torchtitan/models/common/attention/attention.py:336`). The loop also covers the window layers (`traverse` matches subclasses), not just the global ones. Suggested wording:

```suggestion
    # VarlenInnerAttention defaults to cuDNN first; on the 128k global layers it is ~13% slower than FA4.
```

Two small points. This helper has only two callers (`:486` and `:764`), so the `"flex"` default saves one argument at one call site and hides the choice there. Also, `build_model_config` accepts only `"flex"` and `"varlen"` (`torchtitan/models/muse_spark/flavors.py:768`). Consider `attn_backend: Literal["flex", "varlen"]` with no default, and pass `attn_backend="flex"` at `:486`.

reviews.body:
**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** The change touches only the recipe, it is the smallest way to get varlen into the CP-16 LoRA recipe, and the kernel evidence supports it. The only open point is the 16-GPU run, which belongs to the author or a maintainer.

**What this PR does.** `_muse_spark_816b_a42b` now takes an `attn_backend` argument. The CP-16 LoRA SFT recipe passes `"varlen"` and pins every varlen layer to `SDPBackend.FLASH_ATTENTION`, which is FA4 on sm100. The Muse Ulysses CP map gains entries for `VarlenInnerAttention` and `SlidingWindowVarlenInnerAttention`. Without them, `ContextParallelTransform.transform` raises "No CP inner attention configured", because it looks up the exact owner type. The recipe no longer sets the flex FA4 `kernel_options` and `block_size`. After this change, the only flex attention left in the model is the vision encoder's (`flavors.py:560`), and this text-only recipe never runs it.

**Example.**
```text
recipe: muse_spark_816b_a42b_ultradata_lora_sft_cp16_128k (CP 16, EP 16, Ulysses)
before: layers[*].attention.inner_attention = UlyssesFlexInnerAttention / UlyssesSlidingWindowFlexInnerAttention
        kernel_options={"BACKEND": "FLASH"}, block_size=256
after:  layers[*].attention.inner_attention = UlyssesVarlenInnerAttention / UlyssesSlidingWindowVarlenInnerAttention
        sdpa_backends=[FLASH_ATTENTION]; window layers get window_size=(2047, 0) passed straight to FA4
other recipes calling _muse_spark_816b_a42b: unchanged (still flex)
```

### Must fix
- `torchtitan_recipes/models/muse_spark.py:836`: the comment blames torch for the cuDNN-first order, but the order comes from torchtitan's own `VarlenInnerAttention.Config` default (inline comment).

### Should consider
- `torchtitan_recipes/models/muse_spark.py:325`: type `attn_backend` as `Literal["flex", "varlen"]` and drop the default, since there are only two callers (inline comment).

### Questions
- Will the 16-GPU CP-16 LoRA run (loss and step time, main vs. this PR) happen before merge? Today the recipe's numerics change rests on per-layer kernel comparisons plus 2-GPU debug-model runs. CLAUDE.md asks for loss convergence on computation changes, and that run is the one direct check of the recipe that actually ships.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Ulysses varlen: after the all-to-all, each rank holds the full sequence for its head shard, so the document-causal and window metadata are the same as without CP. Under CUDA graphs, varlen needs `max_num_documents`, and the UltraData loader sets it to 8 (`muse_spark.py:697`).
- The `traverse(VarlenInnerAttention.Config)` loop matches subclasses. That includes both Ulysses varlen configs and the sliding-window variant, so all 62 decoder layers get pinned.
- The remat save region `attention.inner_attention` is matched by FQN, so attention is still saved, not recomputed, after the backend change.
- The new CPU test is the only one that builds this recipe, and the build is where a missing CP-map entry would raise. That part of the test earns its cost.

</details>

Not verified: the GPU kernel times and the numerics. I couldn't run the new CPU test in this environment either. CPU CI was skipped because the base branch isn't `main`.
